empty.text: No bank accounts that earn interest (an APY).
No brokerage accounts. Retirement accounts like a Roth IRA or 401K don't get these forms unless you take money out.

w2.title: Wage and Tax Statement
w2.reports: Wages paid to you and the federal, state, Social Security and Medicare taxes withheld from them.

conditions.employee: {from} employs you (a full-time or part-time job)

reasons.needed: {type} income. Your employer sends it by {sentBy}.{earned}

1099-nec.title: Nonemployee Compensation
1099-nec.issuer: Each client or business that paid you
1099-nec.reports: What a business paid you as an independent contractor, with no taxes withheld.

conditions.contractor: {from} pays you as a contractor or freelancer
conditions.overThreshold: A single client paid you {threshold} or more in {taxYear}

reasons.maybe: {type} income. Each client who paid you {threshold} or more sends one. The income is taxable either way.{earned}

1099-k.title: Payment Card and Third Party Network Transactions
1099-k.issuer: The payment app or gig platform
1099-k.reports: The gross amount of payments a platform or payment app processed for you.

conditions.gig: {from} is gig work paid through a platform or app
conditions.overThreshold: The platform paid you over {threshold} in {transactions}+ payments, or {necThreshold}+ directly

reasons.maybe: Gig work. A platform sends a 1099-K over {threshold} and {transactions} payments, or a 1099-NEC if it paid you {necThreshold} or more directly. The income is taxable either way.{earned}

w2-or-1099.title: Depends on the job
w2-or-1099.reports: A W-2 if you're an employee, or a 1099 if you're paid as a contractor.

conditions.typeSet: {from} is set as a job or as contract work

reasons.maybe: Set this income stream's type on Budgeting to know which form it brings.

schedule-c.title: Profit or Loss From Business
schedule-c.reports: Self-employment income minus business expenses. The profit is your taxable self-employment income.

reasons.needed: You file it for self-employment income ({names}), whether or not a 1099 arrives.

schedule-se.title: Self-Employment Tax
schedule-se.reports: Social Security and Medicare tax on self-employment profit, which no employer withheld.

conditions.overThreshold: Your self-employment profit is {threshold} or more

reasons.needed: Needed when self-employment profit is {threshold} or more. You're on track for about {total} before expenses.
reasons.maybe: Needed when self-employment profit is {threshold} or more. Your income streams don't say how much yet.

1098-e.title: Student Loan Interest Statement
1098-e.reports: The student loan interest you paid during the year.

conditions.overThreshold: You paid {threshold} or more in interest in {taxYear}

reasons.maybe: Sent if you paid {threshold} or more in interest this year. Interest that builds up but isn't paid doesn't count.
reasons.notNeeded: No payments made on these loans yet, so there's no paid interest to report.

student-loan-deduction.title: Student Loan Interest Deduction
student-loan-deduction.reports: Interest you paid on student loans, deducted from your income. It shrinks at higher incomes.

conditions.paidInterest: You paid student loan interest in {taxYear}
conditions.notDependent: No one can claim you as a dependent
conditions.underIncomeLimit: Your income is under the IRS limit for this deduction

notAllowedFor.dependent: you can be claimed as a dependent

reasons.maybe: Deducts up to {limit} of interest you paid, even under {formThreshold} without a 1098-E. It shrinks at higher incomes.
reasons.notAllowed: You can't take this deduction because {notAllowedFor}.
reasons.notNeeded: Nothing to deduct until you've paid interest.

1099-int.title: Interest Income
1099-int.reports: Interest a bank paid you during the year.

conditions.earnsInterest: You have an account at {from} that earns interest
conditions.overThreshold: {from} paid you {threshold} or more in interest in {taxYear}

reasons.maybe: {accounts} {verb} interest. The bank sends one if it paid you {threshold} or more; less is still taxable.

schedule-b.title: Interest and Ordinary Dividends
schedule-b.reports: Every payer of your interest and dividends, when either total is over the threshold.

conditions.hasIncome: You have interest or dividend income
conditions.overThreshold: Your interest, or your dividends, add up to more than {threshold}

reasons.maybe: Only if your interest, or your dividends, add up to more than {threshold} for the year. Otherwise they go straight on your 1040.

1099-b.title: Proceeds From Broker and Barter Exchange Transactions
1099-b.reports: Each sale of stocks, funds or other investments: what you sold it for, what you paid, and when.

conditions.taxableAccount: You have a taxable brokerage account at {from}
conditions.sold: You sold investments in it during {taxYear}

reasons.maybe: Sent if you sold anything in {accounts} during {taxYear}, usually as part of one consolidated 1099. Buying doesn't count.

1099-div.title: Dividends and Distributions
1099-div.reports: Dividends and capital gain distributions your investments paid you.

conditions.taxableAccount: You have a taxable brokerage account at {from}
conditions.overThreshold: It paid you {threshold} or more in dividends in {taxYear}

reasons.maybe: Sent if {accounts} paid you {threshold} or more in dividends.{holdings} Reinvested dividends still count.

1099-div.holdings: You buy {stocks}, which may pay dividends.

form-8949.title: Sales and Other Dispositions of Capital Assets
form-8949.reports: Each investment you sold, from your 1099-B, with its gain or loss.

conditions.taxableAccount: You have a taxable brokerage account

reasons.maybe: Only if you sold investments. Some sales reported to the IRS can go straight on Schedule D instead.

schedule-d.title: Capital Gains and Losses
schedule-d.reports: Your total capital gains and losses for the year, short-term and long-term.

conditions.taxableAccount: You have a taxable brokerage account
conditions.soldOrDistributions: You sold investments or got capital gain distributions in {taxYear}

reasons.maybe: Only if you sold investments or got capital gain distributions you can't report straight on your 1040.
